claims.statement: The admin route-plotting save is orchestrated by RouteWorkspaceProvider: a single consolidated `saveAll` action sets the `saving` lock (which disables the tool toggle, undo/redo, the Save button and the mod+s hotkey), runs the plotting leg `savePlot` first and the route-metadata leg second, and releases the lock in a `finally` block.

`openRoute` is a hard reset of the plotting slate rather than a merge — it cancels any pending snap, bumps the snap generation so an in-flight response cannot land on the new route, clears the snap-owning history pointer, blanks the draft/selection/history/baseline fields, and sets `directionId` to null, which makes the next save a create rather than a replace. The URL `routeId` parameter only seeds the store through an effect; the store is the source of truth afterwards.

Edit state loads in two stages: an instant seed from the cached overview payload via `seedFromOverview`, which populates stops, polyline, the consecutive chain and `pathStopIds`, captures a baseline and marks `seedSource: "cache"` while leaving `directionId` null; then an authoritative detail upgrade that sets `directionId`, the full stop fields and the baseline, but only when the draft is empty or is a pristine cache seed (cache-seeded, not dirty, and matching the server stop ids index-for-index). A dirty draft is never clobbered.

Because the create-versus-replace verb depends only on `directionId`, and the cache seed leaves it null until the route detail resolves, editing and saving a route before the detail response lands issues a create POST; on a route that already has its direction pair the server refuses it with 409 CONFLICT.

The stop chain (`connections`) rather than the `stops` array defines route order: `pathFromConnections` returns the longest connected component with its closure flag, and `savePlot` builds the payload's stop list from `chain.stopIds` whenever the chain yields at least two stops — which is how stops disconnected through the connected-from/to dropdowns are excluded from the save.

`addStop` inserts a placement mid-route between the two stops flanking the click (via `inferDetourFlanks`) unless the point lies beyond the route's ends or is within the 150 m loop-close tolerance of the chain's first stop, in which case it appends; the append path links the chain's last stop to the new stop and re-closes the loop edge, and `removeStop` re-links predecessor to successor, both specifically so a custom connected-from/to chain is not silently rebuilt into consecutive pairs.

`setStopLinks` (the property dropdowns) replaces the edge on the requested side rather than toggling it, treats `null` as clearing only that side, nulls `pathStopIds` and requests a re-snap — so a rewire never leaves the previous road geometry in place as if it still matched the new chain.

`reorderStop` rebuilds the chain from the new placement order and re-snaps but pushes no history entry, so a list reorder cannot be undone; undoing the `snap_applied` entry it produces restores the previous path but not the stop order, and the draft stays dirty because the stop order still differs from the saved baseline.

Snap orchestration is deliberately kept in module scope — the bound fetcher, the debounce timer, the generation counter and the pointer to the history entry that owns the next snap result — rather than in store state, and `requestSnapPreview` bumps the generation before its early returns, so an edit that cannot produce a request still invalidates an in-flight fetch and a slow response can never overwrite a newer composition.

Snap requests are debounced by `SNAP_DEBOUNCE_MS` (300 ms) and their waypoints follow the chain order with ids missing from `stops` dropped and a placement-order fallback below two waypoints; with at least three waypoints the first coordinate is re-appended for loop closure when the chain is closed, when the committed path still closes on the first stop and is trusted via a non-null `pathStopIds`, or when the last edit was a placement within the 150 m close tolerance of the first stop.

Only a road-snapped response (`snapped: true`) is auto-committed as the draft `polyline` together with `pathStopIds`; the `snapped: false` straight-line fallback is recorded as a snap warning and never becomes route data, and a thrown error resets the snap state to idle with `warning: "upstream_error"`.

An auto-committed snap merges into the history entry of the edit that requested it when that entry is the newest and has no merged path yet, so a single undo reverts the stop edit and the path together; a commit whose path and association already equal the current state is a no-op, and other commits push a separate `snap_applied` entry.

`resolvePendingSnap` is the save's synchronization point: it fires a pending debounced request immediately with the current generation and awaits it, or otherwise awaits the in-flight promise, so a save pressed right after a rewire or drag settles the auto-commit and sees the road path and stop association that edit produced.

`savePlot` applies five client guards before issuing any request, in order: at least two chain-ordered stops; a non-null committed polyline; `pathEndsOnStops` within 100 m of the first and last stop with the loop-return exception; `pathCoversStops` requiring a path vertex within 150 m of every stop; and `pathStopIds` non-null, the same length as the saved stop list, and equal to its ids index-for-index. Each failure toasts a specific message and returns false.

The fifth client guard exists because coverage alone cannot detect a stale path: `pathCoversStops` would still accept a polyline that passes through the surviving stops after a partial undo or a removed stop, so the save additionally requires the path-to-stop association to match the current chain order.

The plotting save sends only the base direction's data — `label` as `To {last stop name}`, `base_polyline`, and the ordered stops with GeoJSON points — to `POST /api/admin/routes/:routeId/directions` when `directionId` is null and to `PUT /api/admin/directions/:directionId` otherwise; the return direction is never sent by the client.

The server's plotted-save path enforces its own gates independent of the client: route or direction existence (404), a present non-empty `stops` array and the two-stop minimum (422), the 100 m endpoint rule with the loop exception (422), and, in replace mode, that `stops` is accompanied by `base_polyline` (422); the endpoint tolerance is deliberately the same 100 m value the client checks.

A plotted save persists the whole pair inside one `db.transaction`: the base row, its stop rows, its terminal pointers, the derived sibling row, the sibling's stops and the sibling's terminals commit together or not at all.

After a successful save the mutation patches react-query caches from the response instead of invalidating: `patchRouteFromSave` replaces the cached route detail's `directions` with `[base, return_direction]` and rewrites the route's overview entry (both polylines and the lean stop list), leaving an absent cache entry absent.

Post-save reconciliation in the store adopts the server's returned stop ids and `base_polyline` through `setStops` (which re-derives `pathStopIds` from those ids, so later name or type edits cannot false-block the association guard), captures the persisted state as the new baseline, resets snap state and selection, clears history, clears the stored draft and cancels the draft writer.

Save visibility is `showSave = routeId !== null && (draftDirty || metaDirty)`, and every undo or redo recomputes `draftDirty` by value comparison of stops and polyline against the saved baseline, so walking back to the saved state hides the Save button while a restored draft — which has no baseline — can never be confirmed clean.

Unsaved plotting work is mirrored to localStorage as client-only recovery state under `komyuter.draft.{routeId}.{directionId}`, debounced at ~500 ms, flushed on `beforeunload` and unmount, and deleted when it is older than its 24 h TTL or corrupt; it is never sent to the server, and the direction save/replace request is the only path for plot data to reach the backend.

The provider's store subscription clears the stored draft and cancels the pending write the moment the draft becomes clean — an undo all the way back to the baseline, or a completed save — so the localStorage mirror only ever holds unsaved work.

A 409 CONFLICT on a plotted save means the route already has two active directions — the create-mode count inside the transaction — not a version check on the row the client was holding. The direction mutations suppress their own toast for it, and the workspace raises a persistent inline banner in the status slot offering Load latest and a dismiss action, with precedence over the draft-restore offer and the restored confirmation.

Load latest forces a refetch of the route detail and rebuilds the local draft from the server (directionId, full stop rows, base polyline, baseline, cleared history, refreshed metadata); because `captureSavedBaseline` marks the draft clean, the dirty-to-clean transition cancels the pending write and clears the stored draft for the current key, so the confirmation dialog's promise that the work is kept as a draft on the device does not hold in general.

The five client guards and the save sequence are pinned only indirectly — `coords.test.ts` covers `pathEndsOnStops` and `pathCoversStops`, and `plotting-store.test.ts` covers snap settling, commit semantics and the `pathStopIds` association — because the admin vitest suite runs in a Node environment with no jsdom and no test drives `saveAll`/`savePlot` end to end.

The server integration suite pins the save contract end to end: a successful POST saves the base and derives the return atomically, a single-stop save and a start-mismatched path both return 422 and persist nothing, a loop ending on the starting stop is accepted, and a second create on a route that already has its pair returns 409 CONFLICT.
